A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same cdViews research. All 16 pages, including equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–D, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original ScanQA and SQA experiments, component ablations, efficiency measurements, and an appendix human evaluation of annotated views.

after.justification: v2 retains these original benchmark results, ablations, efficiency measurements, and human evaluation.

M1.justification: The viewAnnotator, viewSelector, and viewNMS components, training objective, and frozen-LVLM inference procedure are unchanged, including appendix details.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same ScanQA and SQA datasets and retain the same question categories, test scenarios, and annotation-evaluation coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged throughout the main and appendix experiments, including uniform sampling, image retrieval, GPT-4O+CC, and the LLaVA-OV variant of BridgeQA.

E3.justification: Dataset splits, evaluation metrics, model configurations, view-count selection, ablation controls, and the 50-QA-pair human evaluation remain unchanged. No revised experimental setting is reported.

E4.justification: The component and threshold ablations, efficiency analysis, annotation validation, backbone comparisons, caption-generation ablation, hybrid-model experiment, and qualitative cases are retained unchanged.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is unchanged. Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests; the same three human-evaluator accuracy rates are retained.

E6.justification: Table 1 changes the SQA test EM@1 for LLAVA-OV + FcdViews from 56.9 to 56.8. Table S2 already reports 56.8 in both versions. All other results and rankings are unchanged, and no rerun or protocol change is reported.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulations in Equations 1–13, including view scoring, the loss, and camera-distance calculations, are unchanged. No formal assumptions, proofs, or derivations are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about critical and diverse view selection, zero-shot use of 2D LVLMs, and state-of-the-art 3D-QA performance.

C2.justification: Explanations concerning critical views, redundancy, spatial diversity, and weaker performance on certain SQA question types are unchanged. No new limitations or applicability qualifications appear.

D1.justification: Implementation details, training hyperparameters, annotation prompts, appendix fine-tuning instructions, and the code-access link are unchanged.

R1.justification: The references and positioning against 3D-based, 2D-based, and hybrid approaches are unchanged, including the discussion of BridgeQA as the closest related method.

P1.justification: The marginal arXiv stamp changes from v1 dated 28 May 2025 to v2 dated 5 December 2025. Scientific prose, headings, and main-text and appendix organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures, table structures, captions, and page layout are unchanged. The isolated Table 1 numerical correction does not alter its presentation structure.

improvement.justification: The Table 1 correction makes the SQA score consistent with Appendix Table S2 and the retained 3.9-point margin over BridgeQA's 52.9. This modestly improves internal reporting consistency without changing the method, evidence base, rankings, or conclusions.
